title: Xi greets Trump in Shenzhen as first US-China-Russia leaders' summit is set for Thursday
dek: Xi met Putin for two hours and attacked 'rampant' protectionism before Trump flew in from Manila; the three leaders are expected to discuss Iran, Ukraine, trade and AI, with India watching from outside the room.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
US President Donald Trump arrived in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen on Wednesday and was met on the tarmac by President Xi Jinping, on the eve of the first face-to-face meeting of the leaders of the United States, China and Russia. Russian President Vladimir Putin, who held about two hours of talks with Xi earlier in the day, shook hands with Trump at a reception Xi hosted for leaders attending the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit that evening, according to reports.

The three-way meeting is due on Thursday, 19 November, on the sidelines of the summit. China's foreign ministry has said the leaders will have "an in-depth exchange of views on important issues bearing on global peace", but it has declined to say whether the war in Ukraine will be discussed or what outcomes Beijing expects. The US-Iran war, Ukraine, trade, artificial intelligence and nuclear weapons are all expected to come up, according to reports, though expectations of a concrete agreement are low.

## What happened

Trump flew in from Manila, where on Tuesday he held the first Quad summit since 2024 with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the leaders of Japan and Australia. Xi met him at the airport, returning the gesture Trump made when he greeted Xi on arrival in the United States in September, according to reports. Trump attended the welcome banquet with Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. Xi told Trump he wanted to "advance a constructive, strategic and stable relationship", and Trump said he was confident the visit would advance relations, according to Chinese state media reports.

Earlier on Wednesday Xi opened the APEC CEO Summit at the Qianhai International Convention Center with a keynote titled "Forging Ahead with Resolve Toward a Bright Future for the Asia-Pacific". According to China's foreign ministry, he said "unilateralism and protectionism are rampant", called for upholding the multilateral trading system with the World Trade Organization at its core and keeping "global industrial and supply chains stable and unimpeded", and said China would work toward a Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific. He said China's economy had grown 4.6 per cent in the first three quarters of the year.

Xi then met Putin, their fifth meeting this year. According to the Chinese readout, Xi urged the two countries to use the channels between their governments, legislatures, militaries and political parties to carry out what their leaders agree, and said "we must firmly shoulder the responsibilities expected of major powers" in pushing for a multipolar world. Putin said relations were "stable and on a positive footing" and that trade had again reached a record, according to reports.

Speaking to business leaders at the summit, Putin said Western sanctions imposed after Russia's invasion of Ukraine had backfired and that "the previous tools of economic domination and coercion are now a thing of the past", reports said. He said he expected "big potential benefit" from the meeting with Xi and Trump. His remarks came a day after Ukraine said it had destroyed a road span of the bridge linking Russia to Crimea.

## Background

The Shenzhen meeting was first confirmed by Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov, who said in an interview on 14 November that it would take place "on the sidelines of the APEC summit". Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov has said that Putin and Trump would probably speak several times in Shenzhen, but no formal bilateral meeting between them has been announced. Peskov has said sanctions on Russia are unlikely to be discussed, according to reports. The Kremlin has dismissed comparisons with the 1945 Yalta conference as "games of political scientists", while Beijing has described the meeting as of "groundbreaking significance", reports said.

Trump visited China for a summit with Xi in May, and Putin travelled to Beijing days later. The trip is Trump's first to Asia since his Republican Party lost the US midterm elections, and he and Xi are expected to meet again at the G20 summit in Miami in December, according to reports.

The meeting comes as relations over technology have sharpened again. On 16 November the US Commerce Department issued a rule requiring licences to send advanced AI chips to data centres in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil that serve Chinese customers. China's foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said on Tuesday that the rule overstretched the concept of national security and amounted to economic coercion, and that "China will do what is necessary to firmly safeguard its legitimate rights and interests". A day later, Nvidia's interim chief executive Colette Kress said the company was no longer shipping its licensed H200 data-centre chips to China and had removed that revenue, about $2.4 billion in the last quarter, from its forecast, according to reports. Asked about it on Wednesday, Guo said only that China had "made clear more than once" its position on US chip exports.

The US and Iran have been at war since joint US-Israeli strikes in February, and fighting around the Strait of Hormuz flared again this week, with US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island and Iranian drone attacks on Bahrain and Kuwait.

## Why it matters for India

India is not a member of APEC and has no seat at Thursday's table, but most of the issues on it bear directly on Indian interests. The war with Iran has disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, a route for a large share of India's oil and gas imports, and Indian seafarers have been caught in the attacks: one Indian crew member of the LPG tanker Tara Gas has been missing since Monday, the Ministry of External Affairs said this week. Any understanding on Ukraine would affect India's large purchases of Russian oil, and the state of US-China trade talks shapes the tariffs and export controls that Indian manufacturers depend on for electronics components, solar equipment and rare earths.

At the Quad summit in Manila on Tuesday, Modi, Trump and the leaders of Japan and Australia warned against economic coercion and "arbitrary export restrictions" without naming any country. Wednesday's scenes in Shenzhen showed the same US president seeking a working relationship with Beijing and Moscow a day later. India's Ministry of External Affairs had not commented on the Shenzhen meeting by Wednesday evening.

## What happens next

The trilateral meeting is due on Thursday, and a separate Trump-Xi meeting is also planned, according to reports, though no time has been given. China's foreign ministry has said it will release information about the summit "in a timely manner". North Korea's leader Kim Jong Un could also attend, reports said; Trump said on 16 November he might meet Kim in China, and China's foreign ministry said it had "no information" on that. APEC leaders end their meeting on Thursday.

## Key numbers

- 3: leaders at the first-ever US-China-Russia summit, due on 19 November
- 5th: Xi-Putin meeting of 2026
- 4.6%: China's growth in the first three quarters, according to Xi
- $2.4 billion: Nvidia's H200 sales to China last quarter, now excluded from its forecast
- 21: APEC member economies; India is not one of them
